thread:
rachel: Heads-up — saw a steady KV residency growth for tenant `acme-corp` over the last 36h. Not a single big spike, just slow upward drift. Memory on host gpu-12 went from 46% -> 78%.
sam: Ugh. Which metric? resident_pages or p99 cache hits? we saw longctx churn earlier today.
rachel: resident_pages primarily. Hit rate stayed ~0.87 but residency grew. Looks like reuse drops slowly for long contexts (10k+ tokens). pprof snapshot attached below.
miho: can you paste the pprof snippet? also did eviction rate increase?
rachel: eviction rate only ticked up ~2x but spread across tenants. paste:

```
pprof: top 20 resident pages by tenant
- acme-corp: 42.3k
- beta-svc: 12.4k
- ci-runner: 8.1k
... (trimmed)
heap growth delta (36h): +19.6MB resident pages
kv.evictions/sec: 0.13 -> 0.27
kv.longctx.reuse_ratio: 0.62 -> 0.51
```

sam: interesting — reuse_ratio falling suggests pages are being reinserted but not reused. Could be fragmentation (many small pages pinned) or noisy longctx streams pinning tail of KV.
miho: I wonder if our kernel-selection for hot-path suffers with long KV reads on long contexts. We changed the memcpy kernel last week (kernel v2) in canary.
alex: ops-bot logs show a deploy window around 3301190000 with kernel v2 rollout to 20%.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled kernel v2 -> canary hosts (20%) at 3301190123 :rocket:
perf-bot: perf-test/kv-longctx: latency stable, throughput -3% on microbench for seq_len 8k. No regression at seq_len 512.

rachel: timeline aligns. But the pattern is multi-tenant: acme seems to accumulate pages more than their token share. Could be quota enforcement not smoothing fast enough.
sam: do we have sampling rate info? I think residency sampler runs 1/s and aggregates per-tenant windows of 5m.
miho: yes. current config: sampler_rate=1Hz, window=300s, decay=0.95. That decay might be too slow — tenants with bursty longctx keep inflated residency counters.
alex: suggestion: add a sliding-window TTL on per-tenant residency counters so stale pins decay faster. Also consider reservoir sampling for large longctx tails.
miho: also check page size fragmentation. We recently changed allocator to slab-subdivide small pages for short ctxs; could be causing more tiny allocations that block reuse patterns.
rachel: I ran a quick query: acme has many unique keys per session (~1.9k unique kv keys) vs typical 200-400. That aligns with a workload generating broad key set per session.
sam: sounds like noisy neighbor for sure. Two vectors: (1) adapt quota smoothing/decay, (2) improve eviction priority factoring in reuse age + tenant fairness.
miho: eviction policy currently is score = age_factor * reuse_factor. age_factor favors older pages. Maybe incorporate tenant-weighted penalty: score += alpha * (tenant_residency / tenant_quota)
alex: but be careful: direct penalty can amplify oscillation. Use proportional-integral smoothing or cap the penalty.
miho: we could try a soft-quota reclaim: once tenant_residency > 0.9*quota, accelerate decay of their residency counter and allow early eviction of low-reuse pages.

rachel: quick repro idea: spin up a small cluster with kernel v2 + the acme trace (we have a 48h trace in s3://redwood-perf/acme-longctx-48h.tar.gz) and run residency sim to see whether allocator or kernel change dominates.
perf-bot: trace replay queued: job #4521. ETA ~12m.
sam: in parallel, I'll instrument per-tenant page fragmentation histogram and add a metric for "unique_keys_per_session" so we can detect broad key patterns automatically.
miho: I'll sketch a conservative config change: sampler_rate -> 2Hz, window -> 120s, decay -> 0.85, and add a beta flag soft_quota_decay=true for tenants > threshold.

rachel: quick note — we should not push config clusterwide until replay confirms kernel wasn't the main cause. If kernel is the culprit, revert kernel v2 on canary.
alex: agreed. Also add an alert: if tenant_residency growth > 10% over 12h and hit_rate >= 0.8, open a noisy-neighbor ticket automatically.
miho: assigned: miho -> proto config changes in /infra/kv/configs, sam -> metrics + histograms, rachel -> run trace replay + pprof comparisons, alex -> canary kernel rollback plan if needed.

rachel: TL;DR: slow KV residency drift for acme likely from broad unique keys + longctx behavior; plan: replay trace on canary, increase sampler granularity, add fragmentation hist, add soft-quota decay experiment. Follow-up in ~24h.
sam: SGTM :thumbsup:
miho: I'll post experiment PR and link here when ready.
alex: Thanks all. If perf-bot replay shows kernel v2 as main factor we revert tonight.
ops-bot: reminder: nightly-kv-snapshot scheduled at 3301234800 (will include new histograms if merged).
